clue.text: Fair to abolish Sabbath for good … er … god!

indicators.note: the Sabbath letter is abolished and something else is put in its place, 'for' marking the stand-in

parts.note: fair in the sense of just and even-handed
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
taken as written, the setter's hesitant 'er'

explanation.surface: A protest at a decree replacing the day of rest, the speaker stumbling over 'good' and 'god'.
explanation.walkthrough: In JUST the S is swapped for PI, giving JUPIT; the stammered 'er' then finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief Roman deity, king of the gods, is the god in question.

clue.text: Become bankrupt, when parts are traded for experience

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase change places, the second part moving to the front

parts.note: a failing business is said to go under

explanation.surface: Going bust is framed as a lesson learned through hard knocks.
explanation.walkthrough: GO UNDER has its two words swapped round to give UNDER GO.
explanation.definitionFit: To undergo something is to experience or go through it, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Stupid single honour for Croatian tennis player

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
Marin Cilic, the Croatian who won the 2014 US Open

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at the idea of a lone royal honour for a Croatian sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British state award given in the honours lists; Cilic is a real player.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbecilic is an adjective meaning extremely foolish or witless.

clue.text: Studies dissertations

definitions.meaning: short written studies of a subject, or trial attempts
long formal pieces of writing on a topic

explanation.surface: Two near-synonyms side by side, as on a student's reading list.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name written compositions treating a subject at length.

clue.text: A classic, right? Sun's back chasing topless figure

indicators.note: chasing means following, so the topless figure comes first and the rest after it
the first letter of the word for figure is removed, as if its top were cut off

parts.note: a body is a physical figure

indicators.note: back says the letters for right and sun are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: 'right?' asks for agreement, and 'yes' answers it
S is the abbreviation for Sun (Sunday), the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style aside about a topless figure and the Sun newspaper, dressed up as a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' and 'Sun' hint at the tabloid newspaper's page three, but Sun here is just Sunday's abbreviation, and 'right?' is a question answered in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of Odysseus's journey home is one of the great works of classical literature.

clue.text: Downgrading Germany's European proposal

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A German plan in Europe that would lower someone's status.
explanation.definitionFit: Being moved down to a lower rank or grade is a demotion.

clue.text: Gap sells pullovers and cardigans — even tops

indicators.note: the tops of these five words are their first letters, read in order

explanation.surface: The clothing chain Gap sells pullovers and cardigans, as well as tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' looks like more clothing, but it signals the first letters of the five words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an empty interval, so a space is a synonym.

clue.text: Play Nigel Short's hardest openings — such as this one?

indicators.note: to play with letters is to move them around into a new order
the openings of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to play Nigel Short, the English chess grandmaster, at his toughest openings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' rearranges NIGEL to ENGLI; 'openings' takes S and H from 'Short's hardest'. Nigel Short is a famous English chess player.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue itself is written in a language, which the question mark invites the solver to name.

clue.text: Scientist works here with harpoon and cage? Not he

indicators.note: works in the sense of being worked over, the letters reshaped together
Not marks the two letters of 'he' as left out of the mixture

explanation.surface: A marine researcher is pictured with harpoon and cage, then the clue denies he does.
explanation.walkthrough: HERE, HARPOON and CAGE together hold the answer's letters plus H and E, which 'Not he' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: An oceanographer is a scientist who studies the seas and oceans.

clue.text: President's son steals 500 old bricks …

indicators.note: the president's letters take the others in, as a thief carries off goods

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A presidential son is caught pilfering a stack of antique bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick, so adobes are such bricks.

clue.text: … to cast magic over father's new crusade

indicators.note: the rearranged magic letters go over and around the word for father
casting metal reshapes it, so the letters of magic are rearranged

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Continuing the presidential story: a spell is cast over Dad's latest cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis links this to the previous clue's story, but the clue stands alone; 'to cast' is a jumble signal, not spell-casting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous organised effort for a cause, just like a political or social drive.

clue.text: Copy sample evenly

indicators.note: evenly picks the letters in even-numbered positions: second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An instruction to copy a sample neatly and evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or mimic them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: "Massive" British trip hop artist being difficult …

definitions.meaning: Adrian Thaws, the Bristol trip hop musician who began with Massive Attack, records under this stage name

explanation.surface: A trip hop musician from Massive Attack is described as being awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: Trip hop is a 1990s Bristol music style; the quoted 'Massive' points to Massive Attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricky problem is a difficult or awkward one.

clue.text: … in front of the microphone, a number like a rousing song

indicators.note: in front of places the article and number before the rest

parts.note: mic is short for microphone

explanation.surface: A singer stands at the microphone to deliver a big stirring number.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthemic describes music with the uplifting, stirring quality of a national hymn.

clue.text: Drug ring back in Dorset town

indicators.note: back means the word for ring is read the other way round

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a loop is a ring

explanation.surface: A drug gang uncovered back in a south-coast town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county on England's south coast; Poole is a harbour town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Poole is a large coastal town in the county of Dorset in southern England.

clue.text: Moon rocks left this forge as standing stones

indicators.note: rocks is a verb here, shaking the letters of moon about
to forge is to hammer into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Moon rocks seem to have been left behind, faked as if they were ancient stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon rocks' reads as a noun phrase, but 'rocks' is a verb jumbling the word before it, and 'forge' does the same to the word after.
explanation.definitionFit: Monoliths are single huge upright blocks, like those at Stonehenge.

clue.text: It transfers rotations to wellie he'd thrown

indicators.note: thrown as in tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has thrown a wellington boot, sending it spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle wheel is a gear placed between two others to pass on motion without changing the ratio.

clue.text: Manager's racing car problem: Tesla's been stolen

indicators.note: the tesla letter has been stolen, so it is taken away

parts.note: oversteer is a handling fault where the rear of a car slides out in a turn
T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A team manager laments handling trouble after the Tesla car was stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer is a supervisor, someone in charge of workers.

clue.text: After spinner's six deliveries, yorker initially provides breakthrough …

indicators.note: after puts the yorker's letter at the end, following the others

parts.note: a disc is something that spins
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket over: a spin bowler's spell ends with a yorker that takes the wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner is a slow bowler; a yorker is a ball pitched at the batter's feet. Here 'spinner' really means a spinning disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakthrough is a major new finding, as a discovery is.

clue.text: Acquainted with molten tin? That hurts!

indicators.note: molten metal flows into a new shape, so tin's letters are rearranged

parts.note: ouch is the cry of someone in pain

explanation.surface: Someone handles molten tin and cries out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in touch with something means being informed about or familiar with it.

clue.text: … in the '80s, Cook departs after knowing ball's caught

indicators.note: after puts the departs letter at the end
the ball letter is caught inside the word for knowing

parts.note: fly is slang for knowing or sharp-witted
O is ball-shaped, so it stands for ball
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: Continuing the cricket story: a batter called Cook is out, caught off the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Floyd was a hugely popular British TV chef of the 1980s; Alastair Cook is an England cricketer, the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Floyd was the celebrity chef whose television cookery shows ran through the 1980s.

clue.text: Pined for salary received in Japan?

parts.note: in Japan money is counted in yen, abbreviated Y
a salary received is money earned

explanation.surface: Someone longed for the wages paid in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'yen earned' is a Japanese salary received.
explanation.definitionFit: To have pined is to have longed or ached for something, the same past tense verb.

clue.text: Efflorescent answer by Orlando, perhaps

parts.note: Orlando Bloom is the actor, the 'perhaps' showing he is an example of the surname

explanation.surface: A floral-sounding reply attributed to the actor Orlando Bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Efflorescent means flowering, which is what being in bloom is.

clue.text: Stage device returning characters without skill

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned word goes around skill
returning says the word for characters is read backwards

parts.note: actors' characters are their parts
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A theatrical gadget made from characters who lack talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives STRAP, and 'without' means outside: STRAP is wrapped round ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A star trap is a theatre trapdoor that shoots an actor up onto the stage.

clue.text: Betray no sailor in uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue, uprising says the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A mutiny where one sailor refuses to inform on his fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: To rat on someone is the informal idiom for betraying or informing on them.

clue.text: Archer who's on the fiddle

definitions.meaning: someone who shoots with a bow and arrows
a fiddler plays with a bow, so is a man of the bow

explanation.surface: An archer suspected of running a scam, being 'on the fiddle'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' is British slang for cheating, but here it means playing the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a toxophilite; the other jokingly a violinist who wields a bow.

clue.text: Prince shall be undressed

indicators.note: to undress the word is to strip its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A royal command that a prince shall be stripped of his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V in the Henry IV plays.

clue.text: Cryptically, three in existence?

parts.note: the word three is what comes from the letters of 'there' put out of order, 'out' being the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about whether three things really exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptically' warns of a reverse clue: reading OUT as an anagram signal and THERE as fodder gives THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is out there is somewhere in the world, existing.

clue.text: Does comic admit working the cinemas?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters let the word for working in
comic as in funny or zany, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Does a comedian get in by working at the picture houses?
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges DOES to ODES, which takes in ON. Odeon is a British cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odeon chain gave its name to picture houses generally, so odeons are cinemas.

clue.text: God's peach and raspberry slice

indicators.note: a slice is a cut from within, picking a run of letters out of the words

explanation.surface: A dessert of peach and a slice of raspberry, fit for a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Chandra is the Hindu deity of the moon.

clue.text: Pop idol gains 1,000 pence by euro's collapse

indicators.note: pop as in burst, scattering the letters into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000
E is the abbreviation for euro

explanation.surface: A pop star earns a bit of money just as the euro crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' rearranges IDOL with M, P and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to cave inwards, a violent form of collapse.
